LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. Commanders vs. Giants Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Commanders +2.5 (-110) Giants -2.5 (-110) Commanders: +120 41.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The odds for this game have moved towards New York in multiple ways. After the Giants opened as 1.5-point favorites on Sunday night , they are now favored by 2.5 and have much better moneyline odds to win this game. New York has shifted all the way up to -142 to win , as 62 percent of the moneyline bets and 69 percent of the spread bets at DraftKings are on Harbaugh's team. There has also been a slight change in the odds associated with the total. The OVER was (-112) on Tuesday, but that has since moved to -105 with the UNDER now favored. The total remains at 41.5 for this NFC East battle even though these teams combined for 54 points in their tie back in Week 5. A win on Thursday would go a long way for a Giants team that is looking to win the division even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) sidelined. Meanwhile, Washington's chance to win the division hinges a lot on this game, as a loss would put Daniels and Co. four games back of New York without the tiebreaker this season. Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite pick for every game in Week 10 in his Road to 272 column . He’s targeting New York as a home favorite to cover: I may have included the New York Giants in last week's edition of my Fraud Rankings , but my biggest issue with them has been their strength of schedule. Will I be betting on them when they take on teams like the Jaguars and 49ers in the coming weeks? Likely not, but they once again have a game against a bad team on Thursday Night Football when they face the Washington Commanders, and much like the majority of the season, I expect them to take care of business against an inferior opponent. These two teams played to a tie in Week 5 earlier this season, but with it being a road game for the Giants and the fact that they had Jameis Winston at quarterback, I think we can admit they're in a better spot in the rematch. J.J. McCarthy has been surprisingly solid to begin his tenure with the Giants, ranking fifth in the NFL in completion percentage over expected (+5.3%) amongst quarterbacks who have played 60+ snaps this season. It's also no coincidence that over the last three weeks, the Giants have led the league in net yards per play at +1.5. Meanwhile, the Commanders continue to be a poorly coached team that doesn't thrive in any area, ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in virtually every metric. Washington went down to the wire with the Rams in Week 9, losing a close game while gaining more yards per play than L.A. They've shown plenty of fight against good competition and tied these Giants in Week 5 , but probably should've won after winning the yards-per-play battle 6.3 to 4.9 . Wet, chilly weather is expected, which could make Washington's biggest advantage even more important: the ground game. picks.blurb: New York Giants vs. Washington Commanders: Week 10 staff picks and predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day New York Giants vs. Washington Commanders: Week 10 staff picks and predictions Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants (5-2-1) will take on the Washington Commanders (2-5-1) on Thursday Night Football at MetLife Stadium in their ninth game of the 2026 regular season. Opening the week, the Giants were listed as 1.5-point home favorites, but that line has shifted slightly, with New York now at -2.5 as of this writing. How does the Giants Wire staff see this Week 10 battle shaking out? Here's a look at our picks and score predictions. Dan Benton: Giants 24, Commanders 20 John Harbaugh has made it crystal clear how significant this game is for the Giants. There's no way the players don't recognize that, and they will be looking to wipe away their Week 5 blemish. However, the daunting task of stopping Jayden Daniels remains at the forefront, and how they handle him on the ground will likely determine the outcome. I'm picking the Giants this week, but I am not 100 percent confident in that prediction. This is really a 50-50 game, as are most NFC East contests. John Fennelly: Giants 23, Commanders 20 This could be very similar to the tie these teams played in Week 5, with the exception that the Giants are more settled in with J.J. McCarthy under center. Getting Cam Skattebo back will also give the Giants a boost. Tyler Henry: Commanders 24, Giants 23 The Giants found a way to win in an ugly one last week. Based on how the first matchup went, this game is going to be another close one, and I wouldn't be surprised if we see overtime again. The Giants had trouble defending Jayden Daniels in the first matchup, and I expect that to be a theme once again. I think it will be close, and as much as I'd like to see a Giants win here, this feels like a letdown game for Big Blue -- the type of game that will bring the hype around the team back down to earth a bit. Serena Burks: Giants 24, Commanders 17 Division games are always difficult to predict, and the last time these two teams met, the game ended in a tie after some very questionable decisions by both teams. Since their last meeting, the Giants have fully integrated J.J. McCarthy and the Commanders' defensive front has been decimated by injuries. The spread on this game is only 2.5 points, per BetMGM, but it's probably not going to be that close despite the tie a few weeks ago. The Commanders continue to make the same mistakes over and over, and clock management has been an issue this season. The Giants, despite some injuries, have continued to improve and largely move in the right direction. They currently sit atop the NFC East, and that's not going to change anytime soon. Giants win at home. Kevin Hickey: Giants 20, Commanders 17 The Giants have an opportunity to settle the score Thursday night against the Commanders after their previous meeting ended in a tie. New York should enter this matchup with plenty of motivation, particularly with Arvell Reese continuing to establish himself as a dominant force this season. His ability to pressure the quarterback, disrupt plays behind the line of scrimmage, and make an impact all over the field could be a major difference-maker. Offensively, however, the Giants need to make a concerted effort to get Malik Nabers involved. Getting their star receiver going early would give the offense another dimension and make life considerably more difficult for Washington's defense. The Giants also have the advantage of playing at home, where they can build on their recent momentum. If Reese continues his disruptive play and the offense finds ways to consistently involve Nabers, New York has the pieces to come away with a divisional victory and finally put the tie behind them. It was essentially a foregone conclusion that Patrick would miss at least one game, which is why head coach Dan Quinn confirmed earlier in the week that veteran Nick Allegretti would be the starting center. Allegretti has dealt with multiple injuries since training camp that have limited his time on the field, but the Commanders are confident in his ability to direct their offensive line against a Giants defense that blitzes at the third-highest rate in the league. "I'm excited to feel good physically and get an opportunity to go out there," Allegretti said Tuesday. The Washington Commanders are taking on the New York Giants in Week 10. Check out this Gameday blog for stats, updates and more. Patrick was placed in the concussion protocol during the Commanders' game against the Los Angeles Rams. Yankoff is dealing with a knee injury that has hampered him since last week. Both were listed as non-participants all week. Allegretti, a seven-year veteran with 34 starts in 107 games, specialized at guard throughout his professional career prior to the 2026 season and even started at left guard for the Commanders during the entire 2024 season. He was relatively solid in that span, particularly as a pass protector. In 1,576 career pass blocking snaps, he allowed just five sacks and 13 quarterback hits. The Commanders have options at tight end outside of Yankoff, who only has three catches for 22 yards this season, but Yankoff is a key special teams contributor with 185 snaps running with the unit. The Commanders will need to find a temporary replacement for his production, but there are players like Jeremy Reaves and Ben Sinnott would could fill his role. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch the game Imagn Images The New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will kick off Sunday's action with a 9:30 a.m. game at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins . The victory extended their win streak to four games. Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings . The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers . In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11). The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East. Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to know Injuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Detroit Lions arrive in Munich while riding a four-game winning streak, entering as 3-point favorites against a battered New England Patriots squad at Allianz Arena in Week 10. M y top Patriots vs. Lions predictions and NFL picks look to exploit a massive mismatch in turnover differential and offensive health. I'm backing Dan Campbell's surging Lions to capitalize on a turnover-prone Drake Maye and cover against a New England roster missing key skill players. Here's my breakdown and expert NFL best bets ahead of Sunday's 9: 30 a. m. ET kickoff on FOX. TOP Pick Patriots vs Lions prediction Today: Lions moneyline International games are tough enough to navigate from a logistics standpoint. On top of travel, the New England Patriots have to figure out just who will be playing on Sunday. The injury list is long for the Patriots, with glaring gaps in the pass protection. The offensive line was already missing key blockers and currently has three starters listed as questionable. Quarterback Drake Maye , who was sacked four times in the loss to Green Bay, had words of encouragement for his protectors ahead of this matchup with the Detroit Lions . And they'll need them. The Lions rank No. 3 in pass rush win rate at ESPN , own the seventh-highest pressure rate, and have collected 27 sacks — the third most in the NFL. Detroit is generating this chaos without the normal reliance on the blitz (15th in blitz rate), getting tremendous interior pressure with the defensive line. To make matters worse, New England looks like it will be down its top two running backs. That leaves this offense one-dimensional, and the lack of a ground game allows Detroit to dial up the pass pressure on Maye. International games can be tricky, so I'm keeping it simple with the Lions moneyline and would take this as high as 62% on Sunday morning. Patriots vs Lions combo The Patriots have already been beaten by NFC North teams this year, and the matchup with Detroit isn't easy. New England is lacking bodies all over the offense, and it could be walking into a shootout, considering how bad the Pats' defense has been. Amon-Ra St. Brown just watched the rival Packers pick apart this Patriots secondary, and his projections sit as high as 96 yards for a "homecoming" of sorts for the Lions WR1. Hunter Henry will be Drake Maye's top target in the red zone, with New England's running backs running thin and Detroit getting torched by TEs this season. Lions moneyline Amon-Ra St. Brown 80+ receiving yards Hunter Henry anytime touchdown Patriots vs Lions touchdown scorer: Hunter Henry Although Henry is battling through a foot injury, he is expected to play on Sunday. The Lions' pass defense has been an issue all season, with injuries in the secondary. Detroit has had a rough time with rival tight ends too, allowing the most yardage and 11 touchdowns to the position . Without its top two running backs, New England's red zone work trickles down to the TE. Henry has drawn five red-zone targets for four catches and two touchdowns this season. His TD forecasts for Week 10 sit around 30%. For more Week 10 touchdown angles, including other Patriots and Lions options, see our NFL anytime touchdown picks for Week 10 . Patriots vs Lions player prop: Amon-Ra St. Brown 80+ receiving yards The Lions' star receiver has roots in Germany, with his mother originally from Leverkusen. That makes this trip to Munich a special event for St. Brown, giving him extra incentive to show out on Sunday. The Patriots will roll out the red carpet for St. Brown, given how their secondary performed in a blowout loss to Green Bay last week. New England hemorrhaged huge gains and three TDs through the air. They enter Week 10 allowing the second most "explosive" passes of 20+ yards and are also missing defenders in the secondary, with DB Carlton Davis III out and DB Charles Woods and safety Kevin Byard questionable. For his career, St. Brown is one of the most dangerous WRs versus man coverage and will face plenty of it from a Patriots secondary running man schemes at the second highest rate. This week, they head to Munich, Germany, to play the New England Patriots in a rare above-.500 battle across the pond. Since it's an early kickoff, it's best to get your bets in sooner rather than later, because if you don't have your morning coffee, you could end up placing the wrong bet! Last week was a losing week, as the Lions' defense did their part, but the offense struggled more than I expected. Now two games below .500, we need a perfect 3/3 week to get back above, or at least two out of the three to get back to even. Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook . 1. Jared Goff Over 268.5 passing yards (-112) Lions quarterback Jared Goff is having a solid season so far, and despite a quiet game against the Miami Dolphins last week, I think he will rebound well against New England. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love just threw for 372 yards against the Patriots, the most they've allowed this season. That was at home for New England too; now they are on the road and without their top cornerback, Carlton Davis III. Goff will want to rebound after being held without a passing touchdown for the first time this season last week. With his star wide receiver, Amon-Ra St. Brown, also having ties to Germany, he will do his best to get him a touchdown in front of his home crowd. Goff has thrown for over 268 yards in five games this season, and with New England allowing an average of 231.9 yards per game, going above that by only 37 seems doable with the weapons he has. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85 2. Jameson Williams Alt receiving yards 50+ (-158) Piggybacking off the first point with Goff, I think this secondary, without its No. 2 corner Davis, will have its hands full with wide receivers St. Brown and Jameson Williams. The Packers' top two receivers got over 100 yards each in last week's win, and each also had at least one catch over 40 yards. Williams is a big-play receiver; he can do that on one play, too. His speed will be tough to contain, and even on short to intermediate routes, he can turn a three-yard catch or a 10-yard snag into something more. St. Brown will probably receive the most attention, which gives Williams a chance to break out and take advantage of the lackluster secondary. Williams has only gotten this line in three games this season, and he could've had it last week if he didn't drop a catch. Where Goff can find Williams is in play-action. Goff can have the offense believe it's a run and suddenly, Williams is downfield wide open. When it comes to play action, New England is in for a world of trouble. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $16.33 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown anytime touchdown (-130) As I mentioned earlier, St. Brown has German ties and will want to show out for the "home" crowd. When reporters asked him Friday if he already had a touchdown celebration in mind because of the circumstances, he said: "I don't have it planned yet, I still have two days to figure that out. You know, I haven't been in the endzone in some weeks so I feel like Germany would be a great time to touch the paint again." St. Brown is in a bit of a rut when it comes to finding the end zone, as he hasn't scored since Week 3. Five straight games without a touchdown is the longest he's gone without one since the end of the 2022 season, when he didn't score in the last five games. He also had seven straight games without a touchdown that season. This bet is strictly vibes-based and can sometimes be a bust, but I think the stars are aligning too much for you not to think the Lions and Goff won't have plays drawn up for him to score. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $17.69 If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +286 and $10 -> $38.66 Record: 11-13 Brandon's Bold Bet If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay: Jahmyr Gibbs 4+ receptions (-210) St. Brown over 7.5 receptions (+102) Jared Goff 3+ touchdowns (+225) For this week's bold bets, I am including running back Jahmyr Gibbs, but not for his ground game. The Patriots are averaging at least three passes per game to their running backs, and with the running game possibly limited, Detroit could use Gibbs more as a receiver this week to find success. Gibbs is averaging four catches a game, and he was held to none against Miami and only two against the Minnesota Vikings. I think he gets back on track this week with at least four. Speaking of the receiving game, St. Brown won't just find the end zone on Sunday; I think he will be a go-to option for Goff, which won't be surprising. St. Brown is averaging 7.6 catches a game this season, so I think he can hit eight. St. Brown will want to put on as much of a show as he can in Germany, so he seems like the best guy to lean on this week. Finally, my boldest pick this week is Goff to throw for at least three passing touchdowns. Goff has done this in only two games this season, but I think it'll be a high-scoring affair in Munich. Detroit may have to lean on the passing game and Goff, giving him a chance to score multiple times. New England is averaging 1.5 passing touchdowns a game and just allowed three passing touchdowns to Green Bay. Goff has a chance to rebound after last week's dud and show the world he's an MVP candidate. Odds +573 and bet $10 -> $67.34 Do-it-all parlay If you want to combine all six plays into a parlay and go big, here are the odds: Jared Goff 275+ passing yards Jameson Williams 50+ receiving yards Amon-Ra St. Brown anytime touchdown Jahmyr Gibbs 4+ receptions St. Brown 8 receptions Jared Goff 3+ touchdowns Odds +1186 and bet $10 -> $128.69 Use this information however you like. You can ignore it and watch the game, or, if you want to risk some money, follow these recommendations or test your own luck. The team has not announced if DeVito will remain the starting quarterback when they return to action against the Los Angeles Chargers on November 29. The worst fears of the New England Patriots might have been realized after quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury while playing the Detroit Lions on Sunday, November 15. Maye, 24, will miss "an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season," ESPN reported on Monday, November 16. The quarterback left the game, which took place in Munich, Germany, during the first quarter after he was sacked by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson . Hutchinson, 26, also suffered a knee injury on the play after celebrating the sack. There is fear Hutchinson tore his ACL and will miss the remainder of the season. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel explained that Maye did not immediately head home with the team. Clip of Sam Hartman Flirting With Fan's Mom Resurfaces After ‘Bachelor' News Vrabel added, "Just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel - and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly." Immediately after the game, Vrabel told reporters that Maye would "get more tests run" when he returned stateside. "He couldn't function, couldn't play, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute or function at that level," Vrabel explained. Vrabel downplayed any malicious intent on Hutchinson's behalf, telling reporters, "I don't think it was anything intentional." Taylor Swift Seemingly Skips Chiefs-Falcons Game After CMA Awards Announcement "I'm sure that it wasn't," Vrabel added. "That's part of the game." Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito stepped in and played the rest of the game for the Patriots. The Lions dominated New England in Maye's absence, winning 35-10. "I'm going to continue the process I have been doing up to this point," DeVito said after Sunday's game. "Something that as a [backup], as cliche as it sounds, you have to be prepared to be a starter. So just keep doing what I'm doing, keep my head down, and then if something like that were to happen, you would have the reps and practice and the walkthroughs and everything going forward, so just keep on preparing and on to the next."

away.headline: Patriots captain makes grim admission about Drake Maye's injury
away.blurb: Drake Maye left Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, being ruled out with an ankle injury. And preliminary reports after the game seemed to indicate that Maye's time on the field might be done for the season. "I mean, that's the reality," the safety said on WEEI when asked about everyone needing to step up. "Like at the end of the day, our quarterback's out. He's probably going to be out for the rest of the season. "So once he gets back here, and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer," Vrabel told reporters Monday afternoon. "But I mean, I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye." As the New England Patriots enter the bye week, they await confirmation about their star quarterback's injury. On Tuesday, captain Kevin Byard appeared to confirm the worst . "And the reality of the situation is, is that we're going to have to get behind Tommy Two Chains at the end of the day. And you know, we're all going to have to do more, myself included. Everybody has to play better around our quarterback. I mean, this is honestly before Drake was injured as well. But we got to play better around our quarterback. We got two choices: we can rally behind this guy or we can pack it up. I mean, that's just where we're at right now in the season." On Monday, Vrabel revealed that Maye didn't travel back to the States with the team, instead staying behind for additional testing. This is certainly not the way the Patriots were hoping to go into the bye week, but now, they must use the time off to come up with a new plan. Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook . home.headline: Lions' Dan Campbell addresses celebration banning after Aidan Hutchinson injury
home.blurb: Hutchinson is in his fifth NFL campaign, but this will be the second time in three years that he’s gone down with a season-ending injury. He was limited to just five games during the 2024 campaign after suffering a broken tibia and fibula. Detroit Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson was at the center of one of the most shocking and consequential plays of the NFL season on Sunday in Germany when both he and New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered serious injuries. The play started innocently enough when Hutchinson sacked Maye in the first quarter of the Week 10 contest, but the 2025 MVP runner-up ended up suffering an ankle injury and the two-time Pro Bowl defender went down with a torn ACL shortly afterward. Hutchinson’s situation was particularly stunning given his injury came while celebrating the big play. Former Philadelphia Eagles center-turned-analyst Jason Kelce said on Monday night that perhaps “we should be coaching celebrations a little bit differently” to avoid something like what happened to “Hutch.” Lions head coach Dan Campbell addressed that subject on Tuesday and said there were no plans for anything like that. “No, I don’t believe that,” Campbell said, according to an ESPN report . “I think what happened speaks for itself. We’re not talking to 8-year-olds here.” The 50-year-old former tight end added that the injury was just “one of those things that happened” and used an example from his playing days to defend his argument. Campbell said that he once tore his bicep while pumping his arm in the air during a celebration. “So if you say, ‘Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic’ — this game is built off of emotion,” he said, per the ESPN report. “And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you’ve got to keep your head — then you’re really becoming something you’re not.” “I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let’s be smart. But no, I’m not going to say, ‘Nobody celebrates anymore,'” Campbell said. Detroit will play its first game of the fall without Hutchinson on Sunday afternoon when it hosts the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11 action. The Detroit Lions learned on Monday that star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson did, in fact, suffer a torn ACL in his right knee after jumping in the air to celebrate a sack against New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and landing awkwardly in Week 10. However, the team did receive a little bit of a silver lining, too. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Hutchinson didn't suffer any other significant damage, which should help him get back on the field a little bit quicker in 2027. It's certainly good news after initial reports revealed there was a belief that more damage was done to other parts of the knee, potentially the meniscus. That's exactly what he has become while also establishing himself as one of the league's premier pass rushers over the last few seasons. Hutchinson has 49 sacks in 65 career games, which ties him for the sixth most since 2022, when he came into the league. Hutchinson is also coming off a career-high 14.5 sacks last season and was on pace to potentially surpass that total this year, with six sacks in his first nine games. However, that will no longer be a possibility in 2026 and likely still very difficult in 2027, coming off a serious injury. The Lions will now have to continue on without Hutchinson, which will make their chances of finally reaching the Super Bowl much more difficult. Detroit is currently in first place in the NFC North at 7-2, but the Minnesota Vikings (7-2), Chicago Bears (7-2) and Green Bay Packers (6-3) are all close behind. This marks the second time in three seasons that Hutchinson’s season will end early. He missed the final 13 games of the 2024 NFL season after fracturing his left tibia and fibula in Week 6.

It's been mostly positive on the results front for the Kansas City Chiefs, who come into Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons sitting at a healthy 6-2 overall. Although Atlanta seems to be trending in the wrong direction, it's still in business to compete in a lackluster NFC South. Could that lead to an inspired home performance against visiting Kansas City, or will it be smooth sailing for head coach Andy Reid's group? With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 10 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: The loss of Kenneth Walker impacts how the Chiefs may choose to manage this game, but it shouldn’t change the final result. Kansas City still has the advantage on both sides of the ball, even though Atlanta has punched above its weight twice this season. Ultimately, I expect the Chiefs to navigate through a relatively tough game and return home with the win. Jordan Foote: Being down Walker undoubtedly could make life more difficult for the Chiefs, but rookie Emmett Johnson's been nothing short of awesome when on the field. Look for him to leave attempts at tackles behind on Sunday afternoon and factor into a passing game that has a less-than-100% Xavier Worthy but a new addition in Josh Downs. The real intrigue, in my view, comes on the defensive side. Can Steve Spagnuolo's unit find a way to slow down running back Bijan Robinson and wideout Drake London? If so, putting the fate of the game in quarterback Michael Penix Jr.'s hands seems like a losing formula for Atlanta. It may not be as pretty and resounding as Week 9's throttling of the Jets was, but it should be another victory regardless. Joshua Schulman: Coming off a much-needed bounce-back win at home, the Chiefs will hit the road against a perplexing Falcons squad. They have defeated the 49ers at home and put up 45 points on their division rival Saints on the road, yet they were also shut out by the Buccaneers in a four-interception outing from Michael Penix Jr. Ultimately, I think this will come down to the version of Atlanta that shows up. The Falcons rank in the bottom half of the league in both rushing and passing defense, so I’m expecting Emmett Johnson to wreak havoc on the ground despite Kenneth Walker’s absence. It’ll also be Josh Downs’ first appearance in the red and gold after he was acquired via trade from the Colts. I do think the threat of Bijan Robinson and being away from home will keep this close, but I have Kansas City pulling away in a narrow finish. Tyler Brown: Nothing like a Week 9 win against the Jets to trick the mind into thinking Kansas City turned the corner after an explosive second half, but that might be what happened. Setting aside the Harrison Butker and Josh Simmons drama, the Chiefs looked like an inspired team led by their old faithful stars. Travis Kelce and Chris Jones both posted big performances, and Rashee Rice and George Karlaftis are becoming key cogs in their respective units. A mid-season acquisition like Josh Downs can also provide a shot in the arm for a team. This game will be won in the trenches. Atlanta has Robinson, the NFL’s leading rusher, so the Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers will need a big day to contain him. If they do, Penix, the worst quarterback in the league when facing pressure, will be forced to beat them. On the other side, Walker’s injury leaves the Chiefs’ rushing attack in question. With Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu starting at tackle, the Chiefs will need a big day from Johnson. I think they get it done, kicking the Falcons while they’re down in the same week they traded away their best center and safety. Don’t get me wrong, Atlanta has a lot to play for, just a half-game back in a weak NFC South despite being 3-6. They are getting further and further away from their wins over the 6-3 Packers and 7-1 49ers, however. Published Nov 15, 2026 JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Unanimous in Falcons vs. Chiefs Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons are looking to get back on track in Week 10, but they face a difficult challenge with Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs coming to Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Atlanta has lost four of its last five games and is coming off a disappointing performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Now, the Falcons will have to find a way to slow down another talented quarterback while dealing with significant changes to their own roster. Kansas City will enter the matchup without running back Kenneth Walker III , which could make things more manageable for Atlanta’s struggling defense. However, Mahomes and Travis Kelce remain major threats, and the Chiefs have plenty of weapons to exploit the Falcons’ defensive weaknesses and deficiencies. How will the game play out? The FalconsSI staff delivers its weekly predictions. Scott Kennedy (4-5) The Falcons have had some frustrating games this year, suffering through two weeks of Cooper Rush and a monsoon in Tampa, for example. But last week in Madrid was different. The Cincinnati Bengals simply showed the Falcons aren't good enough this year. Their defense has been patched together with duct tape and one-year contracts, and it simply couldn't hold up against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. General manager Ian Cunningham saw the same thing we did, and rather than deluding himself into thinking 3-6 in a weak NFC South was good enough, he sold at the trade deadline. Now Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce come to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and the Falcons are without All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III after trading him to the Jaguars. Mahomes and the Chiefs aren't as explosive as the Bengals, but, well, they're still Mahomes and the Chiefs... and they're better on defense. We'll see if Michael Penix Jr. and the offense can play well enough to take another step towards feeling good about Penix in 2027, but the Falcons are staring 3-7 in the face. Prediction: Chiefs 31, Falcons 17 Gerald Thomas, III (4-5) The notion of the Falcons playing up to the competition is fading away. Plus, there’s a belief that Atlanta is now playing for draft positioning instead of ending its playoff drought. The Chiefs present too many issues for the Falcons. We all know what Patrick Mahomes can do in the passing attack. And we all watched the Atlanta secondary struggle with Bengals playmakers in Madrid. With Kenneth Walker III out, that may soften the blow against the Falcons’ dwindling run defense . Offensively, Atlanta is looking pretty “eh.” Michael Penix Jr. has gotten off of his heater and must prove himself as the franchise quarterback against one of the top pass defenses in the league. Additionally, Kansas City is top-10 at stopping the run and will likely stack boxes to stonewall Bijan Robinson as the Falcons deal with the key loss of powerback Brian Robinson Jr. Atlanta is looking at a third consecutive loss on the road to the 2027 NFL Draft. Prediction: Chiefs 34, Falcons 21 Garrett Chapman (4-5) The Falcons have lost four of their last five, and the road to snapping that skid will run through the Kansas City Chiefs. The perennial contenders will be without Kenneth Walker, but Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still willing and able to run wild on a reeling Falcons defense that just moved Jessie Bates. On offense, Corey Levin will be taking over at center , and he'll have a pretty difficult challenge opposite him. This should be a tight game, but I'm not sure the Falcons can overcome this team opposite them right now. Prediction: Chiefs 20, Falcons 17 Darius Hayes (4-5) Expects a closer game with Walker sidelined, but Mahomes will ultimately make the difference. Atlanta’s defense has continued to struggle, and the departure of Bates doesn’t provide much confidence that things will improve against Kansas City’s passing attack. The Falcons also face questions offensively with a new starting center stepping into the lineup midway through the season. That transition could create additional problems against a talented Chiefs defense. Atlanta remains competitive, but Kansas City will pull away late to secure the victory. Prediction: Chiefs 23, Falcons 16 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast , (4-5) Despite being only a half game back from first place in the division, it really seems like the clock is ticking on the Falcons’ season. The performances in recent weeks and the trades the Falcons made at the deadline make this game feel like a “crap or get off the pot” moment for this team. There is hope, though. The Chiefs are good, but the Falcons have beaten better teams this year (which sounds crazy given they’ve only won three games). The blueprint for beating the Chiefs is pretty straightforward: stop the run. The issue is, the Falcons have struggled to do that, especially against inside runs, and the Chiefs are an inside-running team. If they can pull it off, the Falcons’ pass defense matches up well against the Chiefs’ passing offense on paper (even without Jessie Bates). On the other side of the ball, the Chiefs’ defense has been solid, but I think they have a real weakness in the secondary with the injury to their rookie Mansoor Delane. To exploit it, though, the Falcons will need to get the run game going. Their passing offense has been pretty ineffective when the ground game stalls. This is a game the Falcons can win... but whether they will is a different story. Prediction: Chiefs 24, Falcons 16 Final Predictions: Chiefs Are the Unanimous Pick Despite differences in the projected final scores, all five contributors are picking Kansas City to win in Week 10. The absence of Kenneth Walker could give Atlanta an opportunity to make this a more competitive matchup, but Mahomes remains the biggest difference-maker heading into Sunday. For the Falcons, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down Kansas City’s passing attack while getting enough production from Penix and the offense. Atlanta needs a win to stop its recent slide, but the consensus among our staff is that the Chiefs will leave Mercedes-Benz Stadium with another victory. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium and will be shown on CBS. Doug Kezirian · Action Network Sun, November 15, 2026 at 4:58 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) will visit the Atlanta Falcons (3-6) in Week 10 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Chiefs are 3.5-point favorites over the Falcons on the spread, with the over/under set at 47.5 total points. Kansas City is a -172 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Atlanta is a +144 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Chiefs vs Falcons predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 15. Chiefs vs Falcons Prediction Chiefs vs Falcons pick: Falcons +3.5 (-120) My Falcons vs. Chiefs best bet is Atlanta to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Chiefs vs Falcons NFL Week 10 Odds Chiefs vs Falcons spread : Chiefs -3.5 (+100), Falcons +3.5 (-120) Chiefs vs Falcons total : over/under 47.5 (-110o / -110u) Chiefs vs Falcons moneyline : Chiefs -172, Falcons +144 Chiefs vs Falcons NFL Week 10 Betting Preview Kansas City Chiefs Preview: Don't Be Fooled By KC's Strong Record The Chiefs are rolling into Atlanta in a very questionable spot as this marks their third road game in four weeks. Despite the brand name and the record, this is simply not the same Chiefs offense of old. Patrick Mahomes suffered an injury to his throwing elbow last week against the Jets and likely won't be 100% for this game even if he suits up. Over the last four games, his average depth of target (aDOT) and air yards have plummeted, sitting at 3.6, 4.7, 4.7, and 3.6. The Chiefs' downfield passing attack is virtually non-existent at this point. They are leaning heavily on the short, dink-and-dunk passing game, and that will probably continue following the addition of Josh Downs . Mahomes is having his worst year by far when facing defensive pressure. If you can collapse the pocket on him, the explosive plays vanish and the offense gets bogged down. Atlanta Falcons Preview: The Buy-Low Opportunity We might have officially reached the bottom of the market for the Falcons . After an ugly showing against the Bengals in Spain, the perception of this Atlanta team is in the gutter. However, the spot and the situational variance favor the Falcons at home. The one thing Atlanta's defense genuinely does well is generate pressure on the quarterback. It is top-five in the NFL in that regard. And When you pair an elite pass rush against this version of Patrick Mahomes who is statistically having the worst season of his career under pressure, you have a recipe for defensive stops. The Chiefs will try to run the ball down Atlanta's throat with Kenneth Walker III , but Atlanta's defense is better than what it has showed in recent weeks. Chiefs vs Falcons Spread Pick, Analysis This is a weird, disjointed spot for Kansas City on the road. The Chiefs offense lacks their usual bite, and they are facing a defense built to exploit Mahomes' current struggles under pressure. The variance and situational angles all point to the home underdog keeping this within a field goal. Pick: Falcons +3.5 (-120) Chiefs vs Falcons Market Trends

Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons , our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 3.5-point home favorites. The Falcons also have the misfortune of not coming off of a European game into their bye week. The Falcons lost 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain on Sunday. They also sent starting safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I do worry about the Falcons' pass rush, even if their defense's other two levels were underwhelming even before trading Bates. With the league's two best running backs facing off, I expect a run heavy day that should lead to a fast moving game. Look for the Chiefs' pass rush to build on their second half against Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix. This will be a game where Atlanta looks game for a couple of drives before the Chiefs overwhelm in route to a victory. The run game will lead to limited possessions for both sides to keep the scoring from getting out of hand. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) The Chiefs and Falcons are on opposite ends of the competitive spectrum in the NFL, and this week's game should show that. The Falcons traded away veteran safety Jessie Bates to the contending Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Despite a talented core of offensive playmakers, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons are only 3-6, largely because their defense allows over 340 yards per game. The Falcons are -8 in the turnover-takeaway category, 30th in the NFL, while the Chiefs are tied for 9th at +4. If they can force turnovers, they will be in good shape to win the game. I don't think Downs will play more than 20 snaps this week, but I would expect the Chiefs to design a few routes for him to get his feet wet in the offense. Chiefs 27, Falcons 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I've got the Chiefs winning this one. Josh Downs makes his debut, and I like Mahomes having another guy who can get open underneath, especially now that Atlanta traded away Jessie Bates. The Falcons also traded their starting center, Ryan Neuzil, so I expect Chris Jones to make life real uncomfortable up the middle. Chiefs 27, Falcons 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) What impressed me most about the Chiefs' 35–12 win over the Jets was how they finished. Kansas City has a habit of letting teams it should beat hang around, and the Jets were within two points at halftime. The Chiefs outscored them 21–0 from there. Kenneth Walker III looked like the player we saw during the 5–0 start, finishing with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. To keep Walker rolling, the Chiefs need their receivers to win against man coverage. Seattle and Denver showed what happens when defenses can load the box and trust their corners to hold up one-on-one: the run slows down, and play-action loses its bite. If the receivers make Atlanta pay for that approach, Walker will have more room to run and Patrick Mahomes can get back to attacking off play-action. Against Atlanta, the key is slowing down Bijan Robinson. That's the operative phrase: slow him down. He's coming off 100 rushing yards and another 47 through the air, so Kansas City has to account for him even when he doesn't get the handoff. Drake London demands attention, and Kyle Pitts can still cause problems for the Chiefs' linebackers and safeties even in a quiet season. But if Kansas City's run defense keeps Robinson from taking over, Sack Nation can build on its five-sack performance by moving Michael Penix Jr. off his spot and forcing him past his first read. I like the Chiefs' chances when Atlanta has to win that way. Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your Kansas City Chiefs head to Atlanta as big favorites against the 2-6 Falcons. Yes, they've lost 4 of their last 5, but this is a dangerous opponent. They've got the league's best RB and a streaky young QB– it's an offense that can get out to an early lead and make things uncomfortable. But, as always, this game will come down to how the Chiefs execute. From the pass protection to the receivers and the short-yardage offense, this team has questions, but they're more than capable. Ideally, they start strong with Walker and Johnson– if the run game gets going, the Chiefs are hard to beat. Chiefs 33, Falcons 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) The Chiefs enter this game after righting some of their wrongs last week against the Jets, although still with major question marks for a team intent on making a Super Bowl run. The Falcons, meanwhile, are on a two game losing skid after their upset win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers. I never quite know what to make of the Falcons. They're a team with some of the best offensive weapons in the entire NFL, yet they can't ever seem to put it all together. Since Jonathan Taylor in week 2, Bijan Robinson will be the best running back the Chiefs have faced all season. The Chiefs have been great defending the run in 2026, and I think they will be able to contain Robinson, but he will still get his yards. Defensively, the Chiefs should also be able to continue the positive momentum they established last week in pressuring the quarterback and leading to mistakes by the Falcons' offense. I'm excited to see what the Chiefs' offense has in store for new wide receiver Josh Downs. I'm keeping my expectations in check, however, as it always seems like the Chiefs onboard their wide receivers slowly. I expect Downs to play 35-50% of the team's snaps, but they will still be able to generate enough offense to take home the win. Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Atlanta Falcons only show up for primetime games; they are garbage during noon kickoffs. Despite having multiple weapons on offense, namely running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London, they can never seem to put it all together in the daytime. On the other hand, the Chiefs are coming off one of their best performances of the season, when the pass rush finally woke up and bullied a terrible team in the New York Jets. At the end of the day, I would expect the Chiefs offense to continue rolling while they ramp up new acquisition wide receiver Josh Downs. Chiefs 31, Atlanta 17 Nate Christensen Atlanta has been a surprisingly competitive team since quarterback Michael Penix Jr. came back. The Falcons have one of the dynamic duos of weapons in running back Bijan Robinson and Drake London. That alongside a decent offensive line has given the Falcons a shot to win any game. Their defense has been surprisingly competent, but after trading Jessie Bates, that will probably fall off. I expect Atlanta to have some nice drives against the Chiefs, but the game will play out similarly to the Jets game. At some point, the Chiefs pressure will get to a pocket-bound Penix and Atlanta won't be able to catch up offensively. Chiefs pull away in the second half. Chiefs 28, Falcons 17 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) If the Falcons hadn't traded away two starters this week, this would feel much more like a spot where the Chiefs could slip up. Still, noon kickoffs have seemed to come with slow starts for Kansas City this year, and this Falcons team still has a reason to fight to stay tied for first place in the NFC South. However, Atlanta has had more letdowns than triumphs this year, including a couple of weeks ago when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran for 342 yards as a team and didn't need a pass to win. This game should be a comfortable win for Kansas City because of its offense, leaning on the ground game once again to stay in rhtyhm and open up the middle of the field for passes. 2026 Standings Nate Chrstensen Maurice Elston Dakota Watson All nine panelists predicted the Chiefs to win by more than ten points. Ron (38-20) and Matt (28-13) had the most accurate Week 9 predictions with only 16 total points of error. Our readers were less optimistic about how Kansas City would perform. Only 50.6% of our readers anticipated a comfortable Chiefs victory, while 37.2% expected Mahomes and Company to narrowly come out on top. 12.2% of respondents expected the Jets to win. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

(Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty Nick Roesch · HEAVY Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:51 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs wrapped their final practice of the week on Friday ahead on their road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Kansas City is dealing with a few key injuries that could impact Sunday's game. The headliner is running back Kenneth Walker III, who is questionable to play after sustaining a groin injury. Of course, when injuries occur, it provides an opportunity for someone else to step up. Joshua Ezeudu Will Start in Place of Jaylon Moore for Kansas City Chiefs vs. Falcons Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore sustained an ankle injury during last week's win over the New York Jets . He has been ruled out against Atlanta after not participating in any practices this week. Getting the start in his place will be Joshua Ezeudu, who the Chiefs acquired in a trade with the New York Giants back in August. Ezeudu was a third-round draft pick by the Giants in 2022. He appeared in 16 games for New York during his four-year tenure, starting 10. A calf injury cost him the entire 2025 season. Ezeudu started for Moore in Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks . While speaking to the media on Friday, coach Andy Reid gave Ezeudu a big vote of confidence. "We feel comfortable with him in there," Reid said. "He did a nice job for us last week, and the other times that he's had to fill in." Chiefs' Final Week 10 Injury Report Here is the final injury report for Kansas City's matchup against the Falcons: RT Jaylon Moore- Out (Ankle) DT Peter Woods- Out (Neck) DT Omarr Norman-Lott- Out (Knee) RB Kenneth Walker III- Questionable (Groin) RB Jayden Ott- Questionable (Hamstring) CB Mansoor Delane- Questionable (Shoulder) WR Xavier Worthy- No Designation (Hamstring) QB Justin Fields- No Designation (Neck) LB Jeffrey Bassa- No Designation (Hand) S Jaden Hicks- No Designation (Shoulder) TE Travis Kelce- No Designation (Ankle) QB Patrick Mahomes- No Designation (Knee, Elbow) WR Rashee Rice- No Designation (Knee) Like Moore, Woods also missed the entire week of practice. He injured his neck back in Week 8 against the Denver Broncos , which Reid has called a "stinger." Delane has also missed the last two games with a shoulder injury that has plagued him since OTAs. Worthy made rapid progress after hurting his hamstring against the Jets last week and is good to go against Atlanta. The same can be said for Mahomes' elbow injury, which gave the Chiefs a scare last week. Norman-Lott continues to ramp up toward making his season debut, possibly as soon as next week. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Chiefs vs. Falcons in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a scary hit in Week 9 against the New York Jets, injuring his elbow in the process. However, Mahomes didn't miss a play in the Chiefs' Week 9 win, and he's off the injury report and expected to start in a road matchup with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Patrick Mahomes (knee, right elbow) not listed on injury report for Week 10. Oddsmakers have expected Mahomes to play in this game from the jump, as the Chiefs opened as three-point favorites on the road in Week 10. They remain favored by three at DraftKings Sportsbook as they look to get to 7-2 in the 2026 season. Kansas City is looking to keep pace with Denver (also 7-2 and on the bye this week) in the AFC West. Those two teams split their two meetings in the 2026 season, so neither holds a head-to-head tiebreaker and will instead rely on division record. Mahomes is a fringe MVP candidate in the 2026 season, and he's put the Chiefs right back in contention after a down 2025 season where he missed the end of the campaign with a torn ACL. The star quarterback rehabbed fast enough to play in Week 1, and he's currently 11th amongst all quarterbacks with 50 or more plays this season in EPA/Play and seventh in success rate. Overall, Mahomes has completed 67.3 percnt of his passes for 2,037 yards, 14 scores and four picks. He's also been able to use his legs despite coming off the torn ACL, rushing 23 times for 85 yards and a score. Kansas City is currently -175 to pick up a win on Sunday, which translates to an implied probability of 63.64 percent. As long as Mahomes is under center the Chiefs are one of the most dangerous teams in the NFL, and they're fifth in the Super Bowl odds (+1000) in the 2026 season. away.headline: Chiefs battled through more injury problems in victory over Atlanta Falcons
away.blurb: “I thought guys that stepped in really helped us out,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. Johnson demonstrated his readiness for more work based on his performance in Denver two weeks ago, when he accounted for 143 combined yards plus a 44-yard kickoff return. Walker’s status for the next game, Sunday at home against the Arizona Cardinals, won’t be known until later this week. Reid announced the injury on Friday and didn’t rule Walker out until the next day. Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13 despite injuries across the offense. Emmett Johnson posted 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two scores. Jared Wiley fractured an ankle, and Trey Smith entered concussion protocol. The Chiefs went to Atlanta for Sunday’s showdown against the Falcons without their leading rusher and starting right tackle. During the game, they lost their right guard and backup tight end. Meanwhile, star tight end Travis Kelce hobbled off the field and center starting Creed Humphrey left the game after getting his eye poked. The Chiefs survived it all, even thrived, in defeating the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 partly because the replacements didn’t miss a beat. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson made the biggest splash. He got his first NFL start in place of Kenneth Walker, who showed up on the injury report late in the week with a strained groin. Against the Falcons he was even better, leading the Chiefs in both rushing — 101 yards — and receiving. He had six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. Chiefs tight end Jared Wiley suffered the most serious injury, fracturing an ankle. That happened in the first quarter. Kelce’s injury occurred when he was tackled after a 23-yard reception. Reid said Kelce, who has been dealing with ankle problems this year, injured his calf. He re-entered the game in the second quarter. “He got twisted up a little bit,” Reid said. The tight end position continued to produce in spite of the injuries, with Jake Briningstool hauling in a 20-yard catch, the longest of his nine-game NFL career. Also in the first quarter, guard Trey Smith left the game and Reid said he has entered the concussion protocol. Mike Caliendo, who had played left guard instead of Kingsley Suamataia in two games this season, filled in for Smith. Elsewhere on the offensive line, center Creed Humphrey took a finger in the face and left the game. Television replays showed a cut under his eye. Mike Nourzad got some snaps before Humphrey returned. Besides Walker, the Chiefs entered the game without right tackle Jaylon Moore, who missed the start with an ankle injury. Josh Ezeudu made his second start of the season. It appeared rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who has missed time with a shoulder injury, may have re-injured himself. But Reid said he should be OK. “He landed on his back, near that shoulder area,” Reid said. “I think he scared him more than anything. He’s going to be all right.” This story was originally published November 15, 2026 at 5:19 PM . Chiefs’ report card reflects

away.headline: Kenneth Walker Injured, Latest Rumors on Chiefs RB vs. Falcons and Emmett Johnson Fantasy Outlook
away.blurb: Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chiefs are going to hold Walker out of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury because they "want to give him a week" rather than try to force him to play through it. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . After being a late addition to the injury report on Friday, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III won't play in Week 10. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the injury is considered "minor" and the Chiefs want to exercise caution with Walker. From a fantasy perspective, Emmett Johnson should be a late addition to your roster on the waiver wire as he gets set to make his first career start. He is only rostered in 33 percent of leagues right now, per FantasyPros . Johnson was arguably the best player on the field for the Chiefs two weeks ago in their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. He had 128 receiving yards and one touchdown on five receptions, as well as one carry for 15 yards in just 13 offensive snaps. Even though Atlanta's defense has been strong against the run, ranking third in EPA per rush, the ability Johnson showed as a receiver significantly boosts his fantasy value. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid's injury update after Week 10's win over Falcons spells bad news for 2024 NFL Draft pick
away.blurb: Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya. home.headline: Chiefs battled through more injury problems in victory over Atlanta Falcons
home.blurb: “I thought guys that stepped in really helped us out,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. Johnson demonstrated his readiness for more work based on his performance in Denver two weeks ago, when he accounted for 143 combined yards plus a 44-yard kickoff return. Walker’s status for the next game, Sunday at home against the Arizona Cardinals, won’t be known until later this week. Reid announced the injury on Friday and didn’t rule Walker out until the next day. Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13 despite injuries across the offense. Emmett Johnson posted 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two scores. Jared Wiley fractured an ankle, and Trey Smith entered concussion protocol. The Chiefs went to Atlanta for Sunday’s showdown against the Falcons without their leading rusher and starting right tackle. During the game, they lost their right guard and backup tight end. Meanwhile, star tight end Travis Kelce hobbled off the field and center starting Creed Humphrey left the game after getting his eye poked. The Chiefs survived it all, even thrived, in defeating the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 partly because the replacements didn’t miss a beat. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson made the biggest splash. He got his first NFL start in place of Kenneth Walker, who showed up on the injury report late in the week with a strained groin. Against the Falcons he was even better, leading the Chiefs in both rushing — 101 yards — and receiving. He had six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. Chiefs tight end Jared Wiley suffered the most serious injury, fracturing an ankle. That happened in the first quarter. Kelce’s injury occurred when he was tackled after a 23-yard reception. Reid said Kelce, who has been dealing with ankle problems this year, injured his calf. He re-entered the game in the second quarter. “He got twisted up a little bit,” Reid said. The tight end position continued to produce in spite of the injuries, with Jake Briningstool hauling in a 20-yard catch, the longest of his nine-game NFL career. Also in the first quarter, guard Trey Smith left the game and Reid said he has entered the concussion protocol. Mike Caliendo, who had played left guard instead of Kingsley Suamataia in two games this season, filled in for Smith. Elsewhere on the offensive line, center Creed Humphrey took a finger in the face and left the game. Television replays showed a cut under his eye. Mike Nourzad got some snaps before Humphrey returned. Besides Walker, the Chiefs entered the game without right tackle Jaylon Moore, who missed the start with an ankle injury. Josh Ezeudu made his second start of the season. It appeared rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who has missed time with a shoulder injury, may have re-injured himself. But Reid said he should be OK. “He landed on his back, near that shoulder area,” Reid said. “I think he scared him more than anything. He’s going to be all right.” This story was originally published November 15, 2026 at 5:19 PM . Chiefs’ report card reflects

picks.blurb: Texans vs. Browns Week 10 picks: Cleveland being treated like an afterthought - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Texans vs. Browns Week 10 picks: Cleveland being treated like an afterthought Chris Pokorny · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:37 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns take on the Houston Texans this Sunday. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers' league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who's allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud's other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston's lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns' permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland's defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns' early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who has 25 tackles the last two weeks, helps Cleveland stick around at home. Below are our Week 10 NFL staff picks:
