Browns fans have had to wait even longer than the Who Dat Nation to see their team compete on Sunday Night Football (their last appearance came against the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 28, 2021). It will have been five years and a day between Cleveland's appearances in prime time on NBC, this time hosting the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) at home. So now it's the Saints left all alone at the bottom. How long will fans have to wait to get the bright lights back inside the Caesars Superdome, or another chance at a prime-time upset on the road? Considering the downward spiral general manager Mickey Loomis has led the team into in the years since Sean Payton left New Orleans (and that being when this drought started), it could take a while for the Saints to find national relevance again. The 7-1 Bills are touchdown favorites against the 2-7 New York Jets, and the experts aren't worried about the quick turnaround. By our count, all 22 panelists at ESPN, NFL.com and Sports Illustrated picked Buffalo to win its fifth straight game. The Bills beat Minnesota 23-6 behind 31 carries from James Cook. NFL.com expects 30-plus from Buffalo Nov 9, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) celebrates after the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images All five NFL.com editors took the Bills , and all five have Buffalo scoring at least 30 points. Bobby Kownack went 35-21, Jeremy Bergman and Dan Parr both went 31-23, and Brooke Cersosimo (30-20) and Gennaro Filice (30-23) were right behind. Parr summed it up by writing, "I don't like the Jets' chances against a well-oiled machine." The average of the five projections is about 31 points for Buffalo. ESPN and SI make it unanimous ESPN's seven experts, from Matt Bowen to Jason Reid, all picked Buffalo . Sports Illustrated's 10-person panel did too in its straight-up picks . Buffalo has won eight of the last 10 meetings with New York, including a 30-10 win at MetLife Stadium last season. Josh Allen has 12 touchdown passes, and Cook has 814 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. Why it might not be easy Nov 8, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs defensive end George Karlaftis (56) sacks New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (7) during the fourth quarter at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Jets have a player who can ruin a game. Rookie David Bailey has 7.5 sacks and is tied for the league lead with five forced fumbles, and New York has recovered a league-high nine fumbles, according to the Bills . Left tackle Dion Dawkins is questionable with a rib injury, and the Bills had to adjust their protection without him and Alec Anderson last week. Buffalo also added Amani Hooker to a secondary that needed help. Twenty-two experts think that's more than enough against a 2-7 team. home.headline: How serious is NY Jets QB Geno Smith’s injury? (Report)
home.blurb: A Monday report provided more detail on the severity of Geno Smith's injury sustained Sunday during the Jets' loss to the Bills.

home.headline: New York Jets QB Geno Smith to Start on Sunday - Report
home.blurb: The Jets also reported that receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and left guard Dylan Parham have undergone imaging tests. Cooper injured an ankle and Parham has a knee problem. Both injuries are something they had earlier in the season, and spent time on injured reserve. No timeline for their return has been established. Geno Smith has no significant damage to his left ankle, according to a report by the NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, and will start on Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers if he’s medically cleared. Smith was injured in the third quarter of the Jets’ loss last Sunday to the Buffalo Bills. Backup Cade Klubnik finished the game and would start the upcoming Chargers contest if Smith can’t sufficiently recover. “He’s good,” a source told ESPN. “He’ll be fine.” Head coach Aaron Glenn wouldn’t comment on Smith’s injury, but indicated that Smith will remain the starter when ready. He dismissed talk of giving Klubnik some development time if Smith is fit to play. Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson, made his NFL debut Sunday. He threw an interception and was sacked three times while completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards. The Jets’ third-string quarterback is former Tennessee Titans starter Will Levis, who is on the Jets practice squad. The Jets may elevate him if Smith isn’t ready for Sunday’s Chargers game. “Geno’s our starter,” Glenn said on a video conference call with reporters. “Come on now, let’s not do that. I think Geno’s had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he’s our starter.” Smith had a physically rough time against the Bills. He was taken into the locker room for a concussion evaluation at the end of the second quarter, then missed the first series of the third quarter. He came back for one series before he sustained the ankle injury on a hit by blitzing safety Cole Bishop. The 36-year-old Smith is working on an expiring contract, and should have some demand for his services at the end of the season, if not renewed by the Jets. He’s 19th in Total QBR (53.3), with 12 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Despite those statistics, the Jets are just 26th in scoring (19.4 points per game) and have not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, part of a continuing problem with red zone scoring.

picks.blurb: NFL predictions: 4 game picks for intriguing Seahawks vs. Raiders matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day NFL predictions: 4 game picks for intriguing Seahawks vs. Raiders matchup Jack Freeman · SB Nation Sat, November 14, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks are hitting the road for the first time in a month to renew their former AFC West rivalry with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday for another must-win game. Seattle enters the game as 6.5-point favorites on the road, their second straight week being favored by FanDuel Sportsbook . While the Seahawks are large favorites, they'll depend on their dominant defense to get the job done yet again as their inconsistent offense is still quite injured. Seattle's "Dark Side" defense will welcome the Raiders' first overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, to the NFL and hope to slow Klint Kubiak's offense, which is averaging 26.4 points per game. Here are four bets/game picks to consider ahead of Sunday's game. 1. Jadarian Price anytime touchdown (+190) While Seattle's rookie running back has battled injuries this season, it's still hard to believe that he's yet to find the end zone. Price has shown the most juice of any Seahawks running back and emerged as a receiving threat last week against the Cardinals. With Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock still hampered by injuries, Price is likely to get a lot of work in the passing and running game against a struggling Raiders defense. Las Vegas' defense has allowed large receiving days to running backs this season, with the worst coming against the Buffalo Bills when back James Cook totaled 58 yards on three catches. While it might be hard to envision betting on the Seahawks offense after they only hung 17 on the Cardinals, a second week with Lock as the leading man should lead to a more complete game plan, allowing them to score and make a statement. 2. Maxx Crosby to record a sack (+144) With Charles Cross out and Abe Lucas struggling this season, there's a near guarantee that the Raiders' star pass rusher will be active in the Seahawks backfield on Sunday. Crosby leads the Raiders with four sacks, and while he hasn't quite been in game-wrecking self this season, he shouldn't need to be to get home against an injured Lock. 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 89.5 receiving yards (-114) Coming off his quietest outing of the year, there's no question that Smith-Njigba should be more involved with the Seahawks offense this week. JSN has totaled over 100 yards in all, but two of his games this season and has padded his total against poor secondaries, which should include Las Vegas' unit. While I already mentioned this in the Price prop, I'll say it again: the Raiders' defense is not good. Las Vegas secondary gives up an average of 234 passing yards per game, one of the worst marks in the league. Even though Lock is still dealing with an injury, JSN should be so open on Sunday he'll only need half an arm to get it to him. 4. Seahawks -6.5 (-110) Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald is undefeated against quarterbacks making their first start, and there's no reason this game should be different. Mendoza has limited reps as a starter and is getting thrown to the wolves against a Seahawks defense that is riding high after holding an NFC West rival to just three points last week. Lock and the Seahawks' offense may struggle early, but there is simply too much star power for the Raiders defense to handle. Las Vegas' defense has thrived on turnovers, so Seattle will need another turnover-free game from Lock and Price like they got last week. If the Seahawks' offense can stay clean there's no doubt the defense will handle Mendoza and allow the Seahawks to handle the Raiders with ease. The Seattle Seahawks have spent the past two weeks dealing with injuries to their top two quarterbacks. That's given Jalen Milroe more time with the starting offense. And head coach Mike Macdonald likes what he has seen. Speaking with reporters Friday, Nov. 13, Macdonald delivered strong praise for the second-year quarterback's work while Drew Lock and Sam Darnold recover from injuries. "I think it's appropriate to say Jalen has done a tremendous job when he's been in there with the ones," Macdonald said. The coach went on to laud Milroe's work ethic, accuracy and decision-making. He specifically highlighted the young quarterback's ability to deliver throws on time. It's a welcome assessment for a player who has waited for a chance to show his ability for much of his NFL career. Seahawks' Jalen Milroe Impresses Mike Macdonald With First-Team Offense Milroe has taken snaps with Seattle's starters during the past two weeks as Lock works through elbow and oblique injuries. Macdonald made it obvious Friday that the extra work hasn't been wasted. The coach described Milroe as decisive with the football and praised his execution when called upon to replace Lock during practice. The comments came in a Nov. 13 report from Seahawks.com's John Boyle . Seattle selected Milroe in the third round of the 2025 NFL draft, taking the former Alabama quarterback with the No. 92 overall pick. His rookie season showed very little game experience. Milroe appeared in three regular-season contests, carrying the ball three times for four yards without attempting a pass. Heading into 2026, he sat behind Darnold and Lock on the depth chart The latest injuries have changed his practice workload, though they haven't produced an official quarterback change. away.headline: Seahawks Get Bad News on RB Following Injury vs. Raiders
away.blurb: The Seahawks could be without running back George Holani when they return from their bye after he suffered a knee injury on Sunday. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport provided an update on Holani, who exited Sunday's 21-13 win in the first quarter and did not return. His offensive role has diminished with Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back, but Holani remains a special teams contributor. Seattle also has Emanuel Wilson available as backfield depth. Wilson was a healthy scratch against Las Vegas . The Seahawks finished with 150 rushing yards, improving on totals of 81 and 120 in their previous two games. Macdonald welcomed the progress while pointing to opportunities Seattle missed to close out the victory. "We've been doing a pretty good job," Price said. "Watching Charbs go out there and make guys miss, break tackles and stuff like that, it makes you want to go out there and do the same. I like where our offense is heading." Just as the Seattle Seahawks were getting their backfield healthy, another setback has put a damper on their win over the Las Vegas Raiders. "RB George Holani suffered an MCL sprain and is considered to be week-to-week, sources say," Rapoport said on X . "Seattle has a bye coming, so the hope is he's not an IR candidate. But will evaluate it next week." Holani has rushed for 117 yards and a touchdown on 37 carries this season, adding 12 catches for 88 yards. home.headline: Fernando Mendoza's 6 sacks shape Las Vegas Raiders' Denver prep
home.blurb: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) left the game after two catches for 18 yards and did not return after halftime. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak called the injury significant but said Bowers was day to day, putting added weight on the rest of the passing game as Mendoza prepares for his first road start. Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza took six sacks in his first NFL start, making blitz recognition and protection communication central to his preparation for the Denver Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 22. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards and added a rushing touchdown in the 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Locked On Raiders host Qiant Myers viewed the debut as encouraging evidence that Mendoza can grow into the long-term answer at quarterback. Myers also focused on the rookie’s difficulty identifying slot pressure, arguing Mendoza must either recognize a free blitzer sooner or ensure the protection accounts for it. The pressure did not erase the positives from Mendoza’s first start. He gave the Raiders an early lead with a 10-yard touchdown run, and the team led 10-7 at halftime. But the offense managed 24 yards over its next seven possessions, a second-half slide that left little margin for a rookie quarterback facing repeated pressure. Myers argued that Mendoza’s presence changes the franchise’s offseason priorities. Rather than entering another quarterback search, he said, the Raiders can use the remaining schedule to evaluate how well they can protect Mendoza, add reliable receiving options, and build a more consistent defense around him. – Kubiak said Bowers’ ankle injury was not as severe as initially feared, but the tight end’s practice participation later this week will provide a clearer indication of his availability against Denver. – Myers pointed to two extended-play Seahawks touchdowns as 14 points the defense surrendered on scramble drills. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s unit will need to finish rushes and cover longer when quarterbacks escape the initial pocket. Average the five NFL.com scores and the Rams win by 9.6 points. FPI projects 11.5. We still picked the Rams in this one when we went through the rest of their schedule, and Arizona is 0-3 at home. away.headline: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
away.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. home.headline: NFL injury news: Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew suffers torn UCL, set for season ending surgery | Report
home.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
home.blurb: India, Nov. 15 -- Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew is set to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing elbow. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported on November 15 that Minshew is planning to have the surgery, although he is still working on the timing of the procedure. The injury is a major setback for the Cardinals, who have already placed the veteran quarterback on Injured Reserve. Minshew's 2026 campaign is officially over, leaving rookie Carson Beck to take charge of Arizona's quarterback room. Gardner Minshew To Undergo Surgery After Torn UCL Injury According to Schefter, Minshew is expected to undergo surgery to address the torn UCL in his right elbow. While the quarterback has not finalised when he will have the procedure, he is planning to go ahead with the operation. The injury occurred during Arizona's Week 9 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on November 8. Seahawks linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. hit Minshew during his throwing motion on the final play of the first half, forcing a fumble. Minshew immediately appeared to be in discomfort but surprisingly returned after halftime and completed the game. He finished the contest with 21 completions on 30 attempts for 166 passing yards. However, the Cardinals suffered a 17-3 defeat against Seattle. Cardinals Place Gardner Minshew On Injured Reserve The Arizona Cardinals officially placed Minshew on Injured Reserve on November 10, confirming that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Before suffering the injury, Minshew had completed 38 of 53 passes for 354 yards and three touchdowns across two appearances for Arizona. His brief stint with the Cardinals included an impressive performance against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Coming off the bench, Minshew threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns, helping Arizona secure a dramatic 33-30 overtime victory. His performance earned him the starting quarterback position, but his promotion was followed by the devastating elbow injury. Carson Beck Takes Over As Cardinals Starting Quarterback With Minshew sidelined, rookie quarterback Carson Beck is expected to lead the Cardinals' offence. Arizona has also strengthened its quarterback depth by signing veteran Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. Johnson joined from the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, while Aguilar arrived from the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad. The Cardinals are now relying on their rookie quarterback to navigate the remainder of a challenging season. Minshew's injury also creates uncertainty surrounding his future in Arizona, as the veteran quarterback is scheduled to become a free agent after the 2026 campaign. For now, the priority will be his recovery following surgery as the Cardinals look to move forward without their experienced signal caller.

picks.headline: Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10
picks.blurb: Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10 Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images | Getty Images Mike Poland · SB Nation Sun, November 15, 2026 at 7:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys return home at 4-5 after escaping the Indianapolis Colts with a nail-biting victory, but the difficulty level rises considerably this week. The San Francisco 49ers are at 7-1 and own the best record in the NFC. Dallas showed against the Colts that its offense can move the football against anybody, but beating San Francisco will require a much cleaner performance, and scoring touchdowns rather than settling for field goals, or worse, falling victim to turnovers. When San Francisco has the ball Everything starts with Christian McCaffrey. San Francisco does not need him to simply line up and run between the tackles, Kyle Shanahan moves him around, gets him involved in the passing game and uses his presence to create space for everyone else. McCaffrey already has nine rushing touchdowns, while Brock Purdy has thrown 17 touchdowns against only five interceptions and ranks among the NFL's most efficient quarterbacks. San Francisco also leads the league in red-zone touchdown rate at an incredible 84%, so Dallas cannot rely on tightening up once the 49ers get close to the goal line. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should take confidence from what it produced in Indianapolis. The Cowboys gained 508 total yards, with Dak Prescott throwing for 335, CeeDee Lamb producing 195 receiving yards and Javonte Williams topping 100 yards rushing. The problem was everything around those numbers. Dallas committed 14 penalties and lost two fumbles, turning what should have been a comfortable win into another game that required Prescott to rescue them in the final minutes. The good news is San Francisco's defense can be attacked. Despite all the talent in its front seven, the 49ers have only 15 sacks, ranking 28th in the NFL. Nick Bosa and recently acquired DeForest Buckner make the defensive line much more dangerous than that number suggests, but Dallas should still give Prescott opportunities to attack downfield. Lamb is now up to 904 receiving yards and is coming off one of his best games of the season. San Francisco also began the week with injuries to their starting cornerbacks and their game status is questionable. If either is missing or limited, Lamb becomes the obvious place for Dallas to attack. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (4-5) I just don't see the Cowboys being that competitive against one of the Super Bowl favorites. In a matchup of organizational dysfunction and well oiled machine, I'll sadly pick the 49ers to win 31-16. Brandon Loree (6-3) At this point, it's probably the Cowboys' toughest challenge and, unfortunately, their biggest thorn in the side since 2021. The 49ers are way better in almost every category compared to Dallas despite having similar if not worse, injury luck. If the Cowboys can somehow pull a rabbit out of their hat and win this game, get ready to hear some outrageous playoff talk. Seeing is believing, so I'll have to see it happen in order to believe—Dallas loses at home 33-23. Dyllan Rivers (5-4) Sometimes the NFL makes absolutely no sense. Teams that have no business winning will go out and upset the heavy favorite. But this is not one of those weeks. Christian McCaffrey goes crazy and Dallas falls to the 49ers 37-27. Matt Holleran (4-5) Until I see it happen I refuse to believe the Cowboys will beat a Kyle Shanahan-lead 49ers team. Dallas does not win back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer and I would be absolutely shocked if they did just that against a San Francisco team that just may be the best in the league. I hope I'm wrong, but I don't see this one being close. Give me the 49ers in a rout, 37-17. Mike Poland (4-5) An entire panel going for the 49ers to win this one, and my head says the Cowboys lose this week to a strong San Francisco roster. But I'll break the clean sweep here so any optimistic Cowboys fans here on BTB have something to align with on the staff predictions. A very tentative and nervous score prediction here where Dallas wins 28-21. And I'm willing to take the hit on this one. Put your prediction in the comments before the game begins.

home.headline: Cowboys injury report: George Pickens headlines good news before 49ers clash
home.blurb: Starting with that is George Pickens, who missed the Week 9 win over the Colts due to a hamstring issue. But after logging back-to-back limited sessions, it would appear he was on his way back to a return, which turned out to be right, as he practiced in full on Friday and is now off the injury report. That's a major return to the starting lineup obviously, but the storylines don't end there, so let's dive into the final injury report after the week of practice. Let's start with a man who has been a frequent addition on these lists: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. Overshown missed Week 9 due to a flare-up in his back and a hamstring issue, but practiced in full on both Thursday and Friday after getting in a limited session on Wednesday. He's now off the injury report and is good to go, which is great news against a 49ers team with one of the best running backs in the NFL in Christian McCaffrey, and one of the best tight ends in George Kittle. So while he is healthy, he will have his work cut out for him. This entire defense will, for that matter. The Cowboys are dealing with enough injuries in the secondary, as Jalen Thompson is set to miss his seventh straight game and PJ Locke is out, too. Also, safety Juanyeh Thomas is doubtful after going from a limited session on Thursday to a Friday DNP. But none of this is the biggest deal on the back end. That honor goes to DaRon Bland, who was a surprise addition to Friday's injury report due to an ankle injury. He practiced in full on Wednesday and Thursday, yet was downgraded to limited on Friday, so it feels like his status is in real doubt, although we don't know much about what actually happened. Porter Jr. did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited partipant on Friday, so he's progressing in the right direction, although he still has a ways to go before we know he's a true full go. The Dallas Cowboys are right back in striking distance for the NFC East title , as one win will give them the same amount of wins as the New York Giants through 10 weeks. So clearly, a victory on Sunday is crucial, but it won't come easy, as the Cowboys are set to host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. If Dallas really wants to win this matchup against a longtime rival, a good start would be getting healthy. The Cowboys have been hit with the injury bug , but the good news is that prior to this matchup, they're getting healthier--as several key players are off the injury report and are good to go. The Cowboys are set to get some key starters back against the 49ers DeMarvion Overshown is good to go for Week 10 Overshown produced splash plays in Weeks 7 and 8 before missing the Colts game. The Cowboys will need one or two of those against San Francisco. Plus, how to watch, what to know, and a prediction Getty Images The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division. Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Where to watch Bengals vs. Steelers live When: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Where: Paycor Stadium -- Cincinnati, Ohio TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings ) Follow Live: Bengals vs. Steelers live blog with analysis, updates, and more Bengals vs. Steelers: Need to know Last time we met The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. The Steelers beat the Bengals earlier this season, but both teams are 6-2 through nine weeks and in position to make the playoffs in the AFC. Cincy has won four games in a row, and Burrow has been on a wild MVP pace during that stretch. Burrow has thrown for 16 touchdowns during this winning streak, adding another on the ground with his legs in Week 9, pushing the Bengals into the top five in the league in EPA/Play on offense. Cincy is heavily favored to win the AFC North because of a favorable schedule down the stretch, but a loss to the Steelers would give Pittsburgh the head-to-head tiebreaker this season. Aaron Rodgers and company are coming off a bye in Week 9, and they're looking to stay hot after knocking off Cleveland (27-6) in their last matchup. Pittsburgh won a division title in the 2025 season, and new head coach Mike McCarthy has the team playing at a high level through the first half of 2026. Oddsmakers have set the Bengals as favorites in this game, but can Cincinnati cover the spread against a division rival? There are a ton of ways to bet on this matchup, and SI Betting has shared game picks, player prop selections and more to help you wager on Sunday Night Football. Here's a compilation of some of our favorite plays for this Week 10 showdown. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Steelers vs. Bengals Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Cincinnati Bengals -3.5 (-110) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers – Iain MacMillan Jaylen Warren Anytime TD (+105) – Peter Dewey Ja’Marr Chase OVER 7.5 Receptions (-125) – Peter Dewey Aaron Rodgers to Throw an Interception (-109) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan makes his favorite bet for every NFL game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s trusting the Bengals at home: I've been writing for more than a week now about how I'm all in on the Bengals , so it'd be hypocritical of me to bet against them in a big Sunday Night Football game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Since Week 4, the Bengals' offense has led the NFL in both EPA per play and success rate, and Joe Burrow is leading every NFL quarterback in virtually every passing metric despite already having his BYE week. The Steelers are coming off their BYE week, but it's important to note that they've had the fourth-easiest schedule in the NFL through the first nine weeks. Despite having a cupcake start to their schedule, they're just 14th in net yards per play, and their offense is in the bottom half of the NFL in both EPA per play and success rate. This game is going to show us that the Bengals are contenders and the Steelers are pretenders. Lay the points on Cincinnati. Steelers running back Jaylen Warren has been one of the breakout stars in the NFL in the 2026 season, averaging 5.9 yards per carry in his first eight games. While Warren entered the season in a committee with Rico Dowdle at running back, the 28-year-old benefitted from a Dowdle injury to take control of things for Pittsburgh. He’s played 72.4 percent of the team’s offensive snaps in 2026, and he should have a heavy workload both as a runner and a receiver in Week 10. Cincy ranks 27th in the NFL in EPA/Rush and is allowing a league-high 5.0 yards per carry. Warren torched the Bengals back in Week 3, carrying the ball 17 times for 127 yards while also adding three receptions for 49 yards. While the Steelers running back didn’t find the end zone in that game, he has scored three times over the last four weeks. Warren has 704 rushing yards, 294 receiving yards and 155 total opportunities (119 carries, 36 targets) in the 2026 season. It’s hard to find many backs with a role like this in an offense, so I don’t mind Warren at +105 to get into the end zone on Sunday night. Ja’Marr Chase is one of the best receivers in the NFL, and he’s benefitted in a big way from Burrow being at the forefront of the MVP race. Chase has 10 or more targets in three of his last four games, and he’s gone off over the last two weeks, catching 21 of his 28 looks for 296 yards. He also has seven touchdown receptions this season, finding the end zone in six of his eight games. I’m leaning with Chase’s receptions prop against a Steelers defense that has been pretty solid against the pass (ninth in EPA/Pass) this season. Chase has at least eight grabs in just three games this season, but his target share is too high to pass him up in this primetime matchup. Rodgers has played well in the 2026 season, but the veteran quarterback does have six interceptions in eight games. That includes a pick against a Cincinnati defense that has been much better against the pass (14th in EPA/Pass) than the run (27th in EPA/Rush) this season. Rodgers has been picked off in five of his eight matchups, and he may have to throw the ball a lot against this elite Cincy offense. If the Steelers fall behind and have to air it out, Rodgers may end up forcing a throw or two that he would avoid if the team was leading. Taking on the Cincinnati Bengals, the Steelers can take the season series against their rival while earning their seventh victory of the season. After a bye week, the team is hoping to shake off the cobwebs before Week 10 action begins. It’s the middle of the regular season schedule, but there is a playoff atmosphere to this matchup. The Steelers can get their seventh win of the year, and a few of these bold predictions might come true as well. Alex Highsmith’s Career Day It’s been a little too quiet for veteran outside linebacker Alex Highsmith. He recorded 0.5 sacks in the team’s latest win, but he hasn’t recorded an individual sack since Week 2 against the New England Patriots. His previous in-game highs are 11 tackles and 3.0 sacks. Against the Bengals this week, Highsmith breaks the tackles record and posts multiple sacks. Jaylen Warren Records Two Receiving Touchdowns Jaylen Warren is the best piece of the Steelers’ offense, and It’s undeniable. He’s one of the best running backs in the NFL this season and he’s single-handedly carried this offense at times. What he hasn’t done, however, is consistently find the endzone. He has just two rushing touchdowns and one receiving touchdown on the season, with two of his total scores coming in the same contest against the Indianapolis Colts. That changes in Week 10. Against the Bengals, I predict Warren will dominate both out of the backfield and as a receiving threat. As a receiver is where I believe he will do his most damage, finding the end zone twice on passing plays. The Bengals might have a plan to limit Warren on the ground, but that’s not enough to keep him from making an impact. Nov 1, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) runs out during player introduction prior to an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Stifle Bengals on 3rd Down Steelers Stifle Bengals on 3rd Down One area the Bengals have been so successful on offense is converting on third down. It doesn’t matter if they have significant yardage to gain, they tend to convert. Senior NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno shared an interesting statistic recently that sheds light on this specifically. The Bengals are the NFL leaders at converting on third down whenever they have at least seven yards to gain. When they are facing a third and long situation like that, the Bengals are picking up the first down 39.5% of the time. It leads the next-best team, the San Francisco 49ers, by nearly 5%. Highest 3rd & long (7+ yards) conversion rate this season: 1. Bengals – 39.5% 2. 49ers – 34.6% 3. Raiders – 31.4% 4. Panthers – 30.0% 5. Jaguars – 29.2% 6. Bills - 28.9% 7. Seahawks – 28.8% 8. Bears – 28.6% 9. Chiefs – 28.2% 10. Lions – 27.9% Lowest: 28. Vikings – 18.5%… The Steelers are likely to put the Bengals in third and long situations throughout Week 10. The only difference between Cincinnati’s previous success and this matchup, is Pittsburgh's pass rush. While the Bengals lead the league in pass touchdowns and third and long conversions, the Steelers are the best team when it comes to taking down the quarterback. It's a matchup of two unstoppable forces, and I'm betting on Pittsburgh's pass rush to limit Joey B and the Bengals to less than a 20% success rate on third down. away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers sign Super Bowl Champion defensive back
away.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed former Seattle Seahawks safety A.J. Finley to their practice squad, the team announced on Tuesday. That moves comes after DeShon Elliott's knee injury on Sunday during warmups that forced him to be ruled out for the game. An undrafted free agent out of Ole Miss the 2023 NFL Draft, Finley started his career with the Los Angeles Chargers before heading to the Seahawks in 2024. Pittsburgh Steelers get great news of two injured players, rule out four others Pittsburgh Steelers sign Super Bowl Champion defensive back - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Pittsburgh Steelers sign Super Bowl Champion defensive back Nick Farabaugh · PennLive.com Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:07 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Steelers also hosted defensive backs Jordan Whitehead and Nazeeh Johnson for visits. Finley was not on the wire for the Steelers has being there for a visit. He was with the Seahawks for three seasons from 2024 to 2026. While he started the year on Seattle's active roster, Finley was released from the team on November 12, which has now led to the Steelers scooping him up. Over his career, he has 19 tackles and forced one fumble. He has mostly been utilized as a special teams player rather than anything else, with teams putting him on their coverage units. If he were to join the Steelers, it is likely he would come in that role as well, with the team only having two active, healthy safeties on their roster right now. away.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . home.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
home.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . For up-to-date Steelers coverage, including any roster news and injury updates, follow us on X @TheSteelersWire and give our Facebook page a like. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage. After all that, the Bolts have the same team heading into Week 10 when they face the Ravens . Los Angeles is the league's only winless team. home.headline: Justin Herbert Avoids Injury After Low Hit in Win Against the Ravens
home.blurb: In a less-than-marquee primetime game at the Baltimore Ravens, the Chargers were able to squeeze out a 23-20 win. They did so mostly on the back of Omarion Hampton, who rushed for 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. The NFL’s review of the play could take some time, and likely will not come down with a decision until next week. That is if the hit meets the criteria, which is questionable. Green hit Herbert below the waist but had his helmet above the knees. Entering NFL Week 10, the Los Angeles Chargers had not won a single game. They were 0-8, had a point differential of -98 and were in the No. 1 spot for next year’s draft. On Monday Night Football, the team finally snatched a win. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has had quite the rough season, although did not look too shabby on MNF. He was 12-for-18 for 129 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions with an 87.5 passer rating. With Los Angeles leading 20-13 with time winding down in the third quarter, Herbert was hit low on a pass attempt by Baltimore linebacker Mike Green. The play drew a roughing the passer penalty, and was posted on X by Rate the Refs. That call was on the first play of the drive, and the Chargers were able to take advantage. They got into the red zone and gave kicker Cameron Dicker a 35-yard chip shot field goal, which he nailed. Herbert was just fine after taking the low hit, and Green as well, but there may be a fine coming the latter’s way. The NFL has notably cracked down on how defenders can hit the quarterback, this being one of additions. Green is in his second season in the league and has never been fined through 27 career games. The standard roughing the passer fine for a first-time offender is $17,911. With Baltimore star QB Lamar Jackson done for the year and the Chargers being 1-8, both teams are looking ahead to the offseason. It has been a disappointing year for both clubs. home.headline: Ravens' Mark Andrews has played through broken hand since Week 3, per report
home.blurb: Mark Andrews is feeling good again. The Baltimore Ravens tight end has been having a season to forget in 2026. His ninth season in the league, Andrews came into Nov. 16 with just 31 catches, 237 yards and a touchdown in nine games. His 26.3 yards per game would be the second-worst of Andrews' career, topped only by the 24.8 in 2025. Most have likely chalked Andrews' struggles up to his age. The 31-year-old has logged plenty of miles in his career, but ESPN's Lisa Salters revealed during "Monday Night Football" that something else has been impacting Andrews this season. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. The sideline reporter revealed that Andrews has been playing with a broken hand since Week 3, but the injury has now healed. Andrews hadn't topped 30 receiving yards in a game since Week 2, when he had 49. The tight end finished with 41 yards in the first half of the Ravens' Week 10 game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Perhaps there was no greater evidence of a healthy Andrews than his diving catch early in the second quarter. Andrews had been listed on the Ravens' injury report since Week 4 with a hand injury. However, he was always listed as a full participant before coming off the report ahead of Week 10. The nature of the tight end's injury wasn't known prior to Nov. 16.
